Sign-in module: server

Source: R/mod-auth.R
aa_auth_server.Rd

Sign-in with login and password protected against guessing (aa_login_gate()), creation of the first administrator on an empty database, auto-login by cookie (if enabled in the settings) and sign-out. The module reports all events to the on_event hook (catalog in aa_events()) and writes nothing to logs itself.

Usage

aa_auth_server(
  id,
  conn,
  settings = aa_settings(),
  on_event = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  logo = NULL,
  cookie_name = "appauth_token"
)

Arguments

id

Module id, the same as in aa_auth_ui().

conn

Database connection with the aa_init_db() schema.

settings

Settings, the result of aa_settings().

on_event

Event hook function(event, user, session_id, value) or NULL.

title

Sign-in form title. Defaults to the login_title text.

logo

Address of an image above the title (for example "logo.png" from the www folder) or NULL.

cookie_name

Auto-login cookie name. Cookies are not isolated by port, so apps on the same host need different names.

Value

A list: user (reactive value, a list with login and role or NULL), logged_in (reactive logical), role (reactive role or NULL), a token() function (the auto-login token of this session or NULL, needed by aa_session_guard()), a logout(reason = NULL, reload = FALSE) function and a logout_all(reload = TRUE) function. Without reason this is an ordinary sign-out (event logout); with reason ("blocked", "deleted", "role_changed", "token_revoked") it is forced (session_forced_logout). With reload = TRUE the page is reloaded so that the modules of the previous user disappear.

logout_all() is "sign out on all devices": it revokes all tokens of the user (event sessions_revoked) and signs out immediately; open sessions on other devices are closed by aa_session_guard() at the next check. Show the user a confirmation dialog before calling it: the button kicks them out everywhere.

Details

If the password was set by an administrator (must_change), the password change form is shown after the correct password is entered, and the user gets into the app only after the change.

Two-factor authentication

With totp_enabled = TRUE in the settings (aa_settings()), a user who has 2FA enabled (aa_totp_server()) enters, after the correct password, a code from the authenticator app or a recovery code. Until then no auto-login token is issued and the successful login attempt is not recorded: wrong codes count as failed login attempts, and the login is locked by the same rules as for password guessing. Auto-login by cookie does not ask for the second factor (the cookie was issued after it was passed). The module reports the events totp_failed and recovery_code_used.

Password recovery by email

With reset_enabled = TRUE in the settings (aa_settings()), a "Forgot password?" link appears on the sign-in form. The user enters a login or email and is sent an email with a link <reset_base_url>/?reset=<token>, and the on-screen answer is always the same, whether or not the user was found. The module itself reads the reset parameter from the address bar, removes it from the address and shows the new password form if the link works. After the password is changed the user signs in as usual: they are not signed in automatically. The module reports the events password_reset_requested, password_reset_done and password_reset_failed. Logic without UI: aa_request_password_reset() and aa_reset_password_with_token().

Self-registration

With registration_enabled = TRUE in the settings (aa_settings()), a "Create an account" link appears on the sign-in form when the database already has users. A visitor enters a login, an email address and a password; the account is created after following the one-time link from the email (registration_verify_email = TRUE, the default) or immediately when email confirmation is disabled. The role comes from registration_role, never from the form. After creation the module signs the new user in. The module reports registration_requested, registration_confirmed, registration_failed and login_success with the value registration. Logic without UI: aa_register_user() and aa_confirm_registration().

Sign-in with Google

With google_enabled = TRUE in the settings (aa_settings()), a "Sign in with Google" button appears on the sign-in form. The user confirms the sign-in with Google and returns to google_redirect_uri; the package checks the signature and contents of the Google token, the organization domain (google_domains) and finds the user by email among already created ones: sign-in does not create new users unless google_signup = TRUE, and then the new account gets the registration_role role. A blocked user does not get in. The two-factor code is not asked for in this case (Google does the confirmation). state from the address is compared with a short cookie of the browser that started the sign-in, so someone else's return link cannot be slipped in. With password_login = FALSE the password form is hidden and password sign-in attempts are rejected on the server. The module reports login_success with the value google and google_login_failed (reason and email in value); on refusal the user sees a generic text. If the page is opened not at the google_redirect_uri address (for example, the app is opened by IP while the return is configured for a domain), the button sends the user to the return address and sign-in starts there on its own (parameter ?google=1): state is stored in the cookie of the site address, and cookies for an IP and for a domain are different. Password sign-in and cookie auto-login work independently at each address.

The role and login are taken from the database, not from the entered string. The conn connection belongs to the app: close it when the session ends.

See also

aa_auth_ui()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "app.db")
  aa_init_db(conn)
  session$onSessionEnded(function() DBI::dbDisconnect(conn))

  auth <- aa_auth_server("auth", conn, on_event = log_event)
  output$app <- shiny::renderUI(if (auth$logged_in()) main_ui())
}
} # }
